title: MapReduce: the model and its limitations

videos.script: Before Spark, there was MapReduce. Two small functions, and a framework that did everything between them. {{two}} Map reads one record and emits key-value pairs. Reduce receives one key with all its values. The framework splits the input, moves every key to one place, sorts it, and reruns whatever fails. {{between}} In this lesson you write both functions in Python, run them with a Unix pipe, and then run them unchanged on Hadoop over a year of clicks. {{run}} Then you read the counters. Two hundred and twenty-four megabytes moved to produce fifty-eight bytes of answer. One argument, a combiner, brings that down to six hundred bytes. {{counters}} And then the limits. A question with two groupings is two jobs, with a file in HDFS between them, written three times. Repeat that fifty times and you see why Spark was built. {{limits}}
